questions.prompt: What does a pipe do to the underlying data it transforms?

options.text: It permanently converts the stored value
It leaves the data unchanged and only changes how it is displayed
It deletes the original and replaces it
It moves the value into a signal

questions.explanation: A pipe transforms a value for display via the | operator without modifying the underlying data.

questions.prompt: In a standalone component, what must you do before using CurrencyPipe in the template?

options.text: Nothing — built-in pipes are always available
Import it and add it to the component's imports array
Register it in main.ts
Declare it in an NgModule

questions.explanation: Standalone components must import each pipe by name, e.g. imports: [CurrencyPipe]; otherwise you get 'No pipe found'.

questions.prompt: Why is the async pipe recommended for displaying Observables?

options.text: It caches values forever
It subscribes, shows the latest value, and unsubscribes automatically when the component is destroyed
It converts the Observable into a signal
It runs only once

questions.explanation: The async pipe manages the whole subscription lifecycle, preventing memory leaks and removing manual subscribe/unsubscribe code.

questions.prompt: Which of the following built-in pipes are impure (re-run on every change detection cycle)? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: async
json
slice
uppercase

questions.explanation: async, json, slice, and keyvalue are impure by design. uppercase is a pure pipe.

questions.prompt: Which character passes an argument to a pipe, as in date____'short'?
questions.explanation: A colon separates each pipe argument, e.g. {{ today | date:'short' }} or currency:'USD':'symbol':'1.2-2'.

questions.prompt: Why should you avoid writing data$ | async more than once for the same Observable?

options.text: It causes a compile error
Each occurrence creates a new subscription (and possibly a new HTTP request)
The async pipe can only be used once per template
It disables change detection

questions.explanation: Subscribe once with @if (data$ | async; as data) and reuse the alias to avoid duplicate subscriptions.
